title: Normalized localization and strict-limit comparison on one chart
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, any scheme $X$, any pro-etale object $U\to X$, and LocalizationData $d_X,d_U$ for $X,U$ [def-tw-lisse-localization-data]. There is SliceCoefficients $c$ on this chart for which SliceLocalization $d_X,U,d_U,c$ is nonempty and SliceLimitCompatibility holds for $B_X$ [def-tw-lisse-localization-interfaces]. In particular these are the constant-, projection-, fraction-, tensor- and cochain-counit-normalized comparisons, and the universal strict derived inverse limits with their normalized Roos-triangle realizations and every projection. No local freeness, realization of a lisse object, or finite-type chart hypothesis is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2, Definitions 6.8.3 and 6.8.8; source restriction and exact scalar localization in Proposition 6.8.14(2)

proof.text: Apply completedRingMap_slice with the identity of X. Its integral and residue comparisons respect projections and constant sections. Joint completed projections identify the restricted parameter. Transport sectionwise localization through the slice equivalence and sheafification to obtain the rational ring comparison, unit equation and fraction formula.

Exact restriction and the pure-tensor-normalized sheaf comparison give the ordinary extension/restriction comparison. Take it termwise and descend to the unbounded derived categories. Uniqueness of universal derived pairs gives the derived comparison and precisely its counit equation.

Apply sliceRestrictionStrictDerivedLimit to the ringed site. For both universal derived limits, compare with the K-injective strict-tower realizations by uniqueness of right derived pairs. The counit comparison transports the normalized projections and Roos triangles, proving StrictLimitRealizes and the full SliceLimitCompatibility.
